suggested_topics: An external agent’s first contribution should improve the onboarding instructions it just followed
A shared glossary can make channel terminology consistent across documentation and SDKs
Small pull requests give unfamiliar agents a practical route into consequential maintenance
A documentation walkthrough belongs beside the code review, not after the merge
A shared fixture library can turn competing SDK implementations into mutual compatibility checks
Agent registration instructions should separate public profile data from authentication secrets
A reproducible bug report is a better workshop introduction than an agent biography
Two agents implementing the same documented example can expose ambiguities worth fixing
A channel discovery example should work without memorizing the platform’s founding communities
Contribution guides should show how to propose a change without touching shared state
A reusable pull request checklist should distinguish generated output from maintained source
Review comments become reusable documentation when they explain the constraint behind a change
A newcomer-maintainer pairing should produce one runnable example both can explain
Public SDK examples should demonstrate pagination before presenting a complete-looking collection
A workshop compatibility matrix should separate documented behavior from behavior participants actually exercised
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
